Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (CI shard sizing / `Test Core` job config); rationale: class (a) — measured twice on the **same unchanged head** (`8c3dd7b39…`) at **30.3 min** both times against a 30-minute ceiling, with three same-day, same-shard sibling controls passing at 20.1 / 25.2 / 25.7 min. Same input, same duration to the tenth ⇒ a ceiling being hit, ⛔ not variance. `Bug`.

⭐ **The step-level reading is what makes this gradeable rather than a re-run**, and it must survive into whatever fixes it: setup / install / package-set computation all **success**; `Run this shard's tests` **cancelled**; `Attest this shard ran and passed` **skipped**; log ends `##[error]The operation was canceled.` mid-stream with **no `Failed Tests` block, no `Test Files … failed`, no `ELIFECYCLE`**. ⇒ Nothing asserted false. And `Restore Turbo cache` succeeded, so a cache *was* present — the overrun is not a cold-cache accident.

⚠️ **The roll-up lies about this, and that is half the cost.** `Test Core` reports `failure` because the shard published **no attestation**, ⛔ not because it published a failing one. Anyone reading only the roll-up concludes "tests failed" and goes hunting a test. ⇒ Whoever picks this up should treat "the roll-up said failure" as uninformative here and read the step list.

⚠️ Likewise ⛔ do not go looking for a slow test. The extra minutes are bought by the **rebuild**, not by slower tests: a `packages/spec` change invalidates the Turbo cache for everything downstream, so this shard rebuilds a large part of the tree before its first test runs. The siblings above touch leaf packages and keep most of their cache. That mechanism is the discriminator, and it is why "which test got slower" is the wrong question.

`priority:p2` — and I want the ceiling on this grade to be explicit rather than implied. The **mechanism** argues that every `packages/spec` PR is exposed, and a 30.3-against-30.0 overshoot means such a PR is a coin flip at best. But the **measured population is one PR, measured twice**; the three controls establish that non-spec PRs are fine, ⛔ not that other spec PRs fail. ⇒ I am not upgrading an inference to a measurement.

⚠️ **Escalation criterion: a second `packages/spec` PR timing out on this shard makes it `p1`.** That is one data point away, it needs no new instrument, and this card already carries the re-check commands.

⛔ **The forbidden remedies, restated because they are the tempting ones and the card is right to name them**: ⛔ do not skip, quarantine or narrow tests to fit the window; ⛔ do not push empty commits hoping for a faster runner. All of those hide it. The real remedies — a larger `timeout-minutes` for this shard, a different package split across the six, or a warm build step ahead of the shard — sit **outside any one PR**, which is precisely why this is a card and why no blocked PR can resolve it from inside itself.

⛔ The one permitted re-run has already been spent on #16376; its result is the second row of the first table. ⛔ Do not spend another on the next instance — that instance is the p1 trigger, not a flake.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code. ⛔ It does not pick among the three remedies — which one is right depends on shard-budget facts this card does not carry.

The card lists three remedies — a larger `timeout-minutes`, a different package split, a warm build step — and ⛔ asserts none. ⛔ This is a technical-ordering call, ⛔ not a maintainer decision: none of the three remedies touches product semantics or a published contract, and none is gate weakening.

## ACCEPT — PR #16868 · a root cause, not the fallback

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat, `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`, 2026-09-08T12:3xZ. CI at review: **36 success · 13 skipped · 1 running · 0 failures**.

### The ruling was honoured — the fallback was not taken

This seat ruled **root cause first**, with a raised ceiling allowed only on a stated reason the rebuild could not be avoided. `timeout-minutes` is **untouched**. The root cause was found instead:

**Turbo folds a run-level passthrough into the hash of EVERY task in the run, not only the task that receives it.** `-- --shard=k/n` is the whole reason a slice gets its own invocation — and it re-hashed the slice's entire `^build` closure, so that leg could hit **neither** the main-seeded cache restored earlier in the job **nor** the builds the shared leg had run seconds before on the same disk. Shards 5/6 and 6/6, the only two carrying a slice, paid that closure **twice per job**.

### ⭐ The instrument does not depend on wall-clock, which is why it settles the question

`turbo run test --filter=@objectstack/cli --dry=json`, compared **plan to plan by task hash**:

| comparison | identical | changed |
|:--|--:|--:|
| plain vs plain (**control**) | 60 | **0** |
| plain vs `-- --shard=1/2` | 0 | **60** — including all 59 `build` tasks |
| `--shard=1/2` vs `--shard=2/2` | 0 | **60** |

Nothing about the *suite* differs between those plans; only the **build graph's hashes** move. ⇒ Rebuild and slower-tests are separated directly, not inferred from durations. The control firing first is what makes the other two rows readable.

Corroborated live: on run `34193080219` the slice leg reported `Cached: 2 cached, 58 total` / `9m18.941s` while `@objectstack/cli:test` measured `Duration 187.49s` — roughly six of nine minutes were duplicate rebuild.

### Verified by this seat, not taken on the report

- **`--only` is present** in the sliced test leg (`ci.yml:646`) — the half that makes the new build step load-bearing rather than additive.
- **`timeout-minutes: 45`** at `ci.yml:316`. ⇒ The dev is right and **this card's title is stale**: the "30-minute ceiling" was raised by #16173. The acute blockage is gone; the defect it was a symptom of was not.
- **Fail-closed**: the new step carries no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` guard, so a failed closure build fails the job and the test leg never runs. The dev's harness measured the real exit status (17) propagating and no attestation published.

### ⚠️ A3 falsified, and it removes the competing explanation

**Shard 5/6 does NOT carry `@objectstack/spec`** — spec is on shard 1/6. 5/6 carries `@objectstack/cli 1/2` plus ten leaf packages, verified by running the shard selector for all six. ⇒ The reading the card's phrasing invites — *"spec's own heavy suite only runs when spec changes, so this shard is slower"* — is **false**, and the slice leg is left as the discriminator.

### ⚠️ The one thing a reviewer must not misread, and the dev named it first

**This PR's own CI run does not exercise the change.** `turbo ls --affected` returns **0 packages** for a `.github/**`-only diff, so every shard takes the *"nothing to test"* exit and the new step short-circuits. ⇒ A green `Test Core` here carries **no information** about the new path, and this ACCEPT does ⛔ not rest on one. It rests on the dry-run hash comparison, the local back-to-back replay (`5 cached, 57 total` / `3m45.918s` → `57 cached, 57 total` / `153ms >>> FULL TURBO`), and an offline harness driving the extracted step bodies over four shard shapes including the failing-build case.

The first run that truly exercises this is one whose affected set reaches `@objectstack/cli` — a merge-group run, or the next `packages/spec` PR. **That is the run to watch after this lands.**

⭐ A gate did real work here: `check:stall-guard-headroom` **refused a verdict** when the first shape put two guarded runs in one step, because a guarded site is the triple (file, job, step) and refusing beats judging two runs against the worst reading of their union. It named the fix; the PR took it.

### Next

Path face clean (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`; not governed, not the contract face). Ordinary route: flip and enqueue once `Lint & Repo Gates` completes.

Run **34239039069** (`CI`, `push` on `main`, created 2026-09-08T14:33:37Z — the run produced by #16880's merge). `@objectstack/cli` depends on `@objectstack/lint` (read from `packages/cli/package.json`), so that PR's `packages/lint/src/**` diff put the CLI in the affected set. ⇒ this is the first run to exercise #16868's change.

⭐ **The correction first: the sliced legs are not separate jobs.** `ci.yml:629` loops `for LEG in __whole__ $SLICES` *inside* each `Test Core (k/6)` job. My earlier note said to look for a slice job; that was wrong, and `Dogfood Verify CLI` is not it. The reading below comes from the jobs' **step records**.

### Measured — the new step, across all six shards

| shard | `Build the sliced package's dependency closure` | `Run this shard's tests` |
|---|---|---|
| 1/6 | success **0s** | 576s |
| 2/6 | success **0s** | 732s |
| 3/6 | success **0s** | 830s |
| 4/6 | success **0s** | 656s |
| 5/6 | success **366s** | 315s |
| 6/6 | success **371s** | 270s |

⇒ The step exists, ran on **6 of 6** shards, and **discriminates**: it does real work (366 s / 371 s) on exactly the two shards that carry a sliced package, and short-circuits to 0 s on the four that do not — the `if [ ! -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/shard-packages.txt" ]` guard at `:516`. ⭐ That 371 s / 0 s split **is** the firing control: a step that ran 0 s everywhere would be indistinguishable from a step that is wired but dead.

Corroborating, independent of the durations: shard 6 uploaded **2 files** into `test-core-run-summary-6-of-6` while shard 1 uploaded **1** — two turbo run summaries on 6, one on 1. ⇒ two legs ran on the sliced shard, one on the unsliced.

### ⛔ What this does NOT yet show, stated plainly

- **The slice leg's own `Cached: N cached, M total` is still unread.** The whole-leg figure I did read (shard 1) is `Tasks: 48 successful, 48 total` / `Cached: 1 cached, 48 total` — that is the `__whole__` leg, ⛔ not the slice leg, so it does not answer the question.
- ⚠️ **And on this run it would not have been the interesting number anyway.** The build steps took 366–371 s, i.e. they built **cold** — which is exactly right for the *first* run after the change: nothing passthrough-free was in the cache to hit yet. This run **populates** that cache. The saving appears on the **next** run whose slice covers the same closure. ⇒ Claiming a cache win from this run would have been claiming the thing the run cannot show.
- ⚠️ **Channel limit, recorded rather than worked around:** this container cannot download run-summary artifacts — they redirect to `productionresultssa1.blob.core.windows.net`, which the egress proxy refuses (`CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`). Job logs are reachable only through the MCP tail. That is why the figure above is a step-record reading and not a summary-file reading.

### Still owed on this card

The slice leg's `Cached: N cached, M total` on the **next** run whose sliced package set covers the closure this run just built. I will read it there and post it here. ⛔ Until then the quantitative half of #16395's claim is unproven, and I am not calling it proven.
